title: Buck and the Sled Team
text:
In Jack London's novel, Buck, a big dog stolen from a California ranch, was sold into a sled team in the Yukon during the Klondike gold rush. The team carried mail for two French Canadian couriers, Francois and Perrault, and its lead dog was Spitz, a hard, experienced fighter who kept order with his teeth.

Buck learned the work quickly and came to hate Spitz. Instead of challenging him openly, he began to undermine him, stepping in to protect dogs that Spitz was punishing. Discipline broke down. The other dogs grew lazy and quarrelsome, the team stopped pulling together, and the sled slowed. Fights broke out constantly.

At last Buck and Spitz fought to the death in the snow, and Buck won. The next morning Francois tried to put another dog in the lead, but Buck would not allow it, and finally the men gave him the place.

As leader Buck surprised them. He punished the slackers, broke up the fighting, and brought the team back into line. Every dog pulled its weight again. The team, now working as one, made a record run back to Skagway, covering the trail in fourteen days at an average of forty miles a day.
lesson: A team where members fight for position stops moving forward. A leader earns the role by restoring order and making everyone pull together, not just by winning the fight.
people: Buck, Spitz, Francois, Perrault, the sled dogs
location: United States (novel set in the Yukon, Canada)
source: Jack London, The Call of the Wild (1903), chapters 3 and 4
